title: After-hours places in Toledo, Cleveland and Los Angeles
summary: Wilson recalls beer served in aluminum saucepans, Alberta's after-hours club in Toledo, and Hinton adds Lovejoy's on Central Avenue.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Yes sir -- many wonderful evenings and mornings and early mornings with Art in Toledo and some of his friends, and in one of the places where he used to like to play the piano so much, and they served beer -- beer was his specialty, ice cold beer in --
No, that's in Cleveland, I'm talking about Toledo now.
In a little saucepan, an aluminum saucepan is what they served it in, a little saucepan would hold about a pint of beer, or something.

And in that little saucepan, the aluminum would come frosted, with that cold beer and the cold beer in that cold pan was just delicious, and we'd play the piano and drink that beer on hot summer evenings there in Toledo.
Another lady who you might know from the London House in Chicago -- Alberta, she later took care of the ladies room at the London House some years ago.
Oh yes! She was -- yes, I remember her, sure.
Well, she had an after hours club in Toledo and she had one of Art's favorite old upright pianos in her place, and Alberta's was one of our regular stops.
Uh huh. Even Lovejoy's Out in Los Angeles, in the thirties? I played at Lovejoys in California, they had an upright piano there. The guy, Lovejoy, he used to be a comedian or something in New York.
He had a little after hours bar on Central Avenue, in LA.
Uh huh. Of course, one of the most famous ones that Art really liked was the one in Cleveland, Val's.
